title: Risk budgeting rollout wizard - draft notes
body:
Purpose
- Sketch and capture UX decisions for a rollout wizard that centers an explicit risk budget concept rather than only percent traffic. Goal is to give operators a clear, measurable safety allowance and reduce cognitive load when creating canary and A/B experiments.
- Focus scope: new wizard screens, risk budget slider, safety checks, auto-fallback policy composer, preview/dry-run states, and minimal operator microcopy.

Context and motivation
- Operators increasingly ask for an explicit metric they can reason about when doing progressive rollouts. Percent traffic is useful but implicit risk is hard to quantify when experiments change model families, quantization, or region.
- Existing console flows focus on traffic slices and health checks; we need a complementary flow where the user sets an allowable risk budget (e.g., 0.5% error budget, 1000 additional latency-ms aggregate) and the system converts that into traffic schedule suggestions and automatic guardrails.
- This doc is intentionally rough, intended for discussion in grooming and scoping sessions.

Persona and journey summary
- Operator: platform engineer or product ML owner running a model change across production. Wants predictable safety, low operational overhead, and clear indicators to pause/rollback.
- Primary success criteria: launch a canary with an explicit risk budget, observe metrics with a real-time consumption meter, and have auto-fallback trigger reliably under configured thresholds.

Wizard flow (high level)
1) Entry: select rollout type
   - Options: Canary, A/B test, Percent-scheduled rollout
   - Quick tip line: Use risk budget to bound measurable regressions while testing new model code or weights.
2) Choose baseline and candidate models
   - Model pinning UI, version picker, region targets. Show small diff summary: token cost delta, expected latency delta (based on model profile).
3) Define risk budget (new)
   - Slider + manual entry: risk budget expressed as a composite budget or single metric. Examples: percent error budget, absolute downstream failures, aggregate latency budget in ms-tokens.
   - Suggested presets: conservative, balanced, exploratory. Preset maps to internal policies for rollout speed and fallback thresholds.
   - Inline help: short definition and example mapping to percent traffic.
4) Safety checks and required signals
   - Required signals: p95 latency, error rate, semantic regression score, failed-evals fraction. Operator can add optional custom signals (from existing evals or metrics).
   - Default: p95 and error rate required.
5) Schedule and traffic recommendation
   - System suggests a traffic schedule that consumes the budget linearly over N steps or via an adaptive policy that slows when budget consumption spikes.
   - UI shows an interactive chart: X axis = time / steps, Y axis = traffic %, with an overlay of projected budget consumption.
6) Auto-fallback policy composer
   - Build policy blocks: immediate fallback, step pause + operator notification, step revert to previous model, or route to degraded variant.
   - Microcopy for toggles: when enabled, automatic fallback will switch traffic back to last healthy model if selected signals exceed thresholds.
7) Preview, dry-run, and guardrail summary
   - Dry-run mode simulates budget consumption based on recent traffic and synthetic perturbations. Preview shows worst-case and median projected budget usage.
8) Launch and monitoring hooks
   - Suggestions for alerting channels, annotation templates, and required postmortem triggers if budget exhausted.

Wireframe and UI notes (low-fidelity)
- Top header: two-line summary card: model pair, risk budget summary (amount left), projected end time at current rate.
- Risk budget control: large slider 0-5% for error budget or numeric input for custom units. Color states: green (safe), amber (consuming), red (exhausted).
- Real-time meter: small horizontal progress bar with numeric tooltip showing consumed vs allowed.
- Chart area: stacked view with projected budget consumption bands, current traces, and hover to show per-step expected delta.
- Fallback composer: drag-and-drop policy blocks, each block has small form for threshold config and action. Allow inline test button that runs a dry-run for that block.
- Confirmation modal: clear irreversible steps call out, show Safeguards: automatic reversion, circuit-breaker limits.

Microcopy examples
- Risk budget label helper: The maximum amount of measurable regressions you allow while we ramp traffic. If the budget is exceeded we will automatically rollback or pause per your policy.
- Preset explanation: Conservative uses small steps and tight thresholds for production critical services.

Edge cases and open questions
- What unit should be primary by default? Error rate percent is simplest but teams also want latency budgets and semantic regression units. We need a single primary unit on the UI with advanced toggles for other signals.
- How to communicate composite budgets? Consider showing normalized consumption and per-signal breakdown.
- Interaction with existing traffic-slicing features and experiment labels. Ensure compatibility with A/B experiment analytics pipelines.
- Ok to auto-convert risk budget to a traffic schedule? Operators should be able to override.

Backlog grooming items (candidate jira tickets)
- ROLL-3421: risk budget control component and presets (UX + frontend)
- ROLL-3422: budget consumption simulation engine (backend)
- ROLL-3423: fallback composer UI and actions integration
- ROLL-3424: preview/dry-run mode and projection charts
- ROLL-3425: alerts and annotation templates for exhausted budgets
- Notes: prioritize ROLL-3421 and ROLL-3422 for initial alpha.

Acceptance criteria for alpha
- Operator can create a canary using the wizard, set a numeric risk budget, and launch in dry-run or live mode.
- System produces a suggested traffic schedule and shows projected budget consumption in preview.
- Auto-fallback block can be created and saved; if simulated thresholds are breached during dry-run, the action is indicated as triggered in preview.

Next steps and owners
- Spike for backend simulation engine: Jonah Park ( ETA 2 weeks )
- Proto UI components: Evan Carter and Mina Alvarez (ETA 3 weeks)
- Product review and gating: Priya Das to coordinate with SRE and Applied ML for required signals
- Schedule 60 minute grooming on next product sync; agenda: clarify primary unit, presets, and rollout preview UX.

Misc scratchpad TODOs
- Add concrete examples mapping budgets to traffic percents for typical model deltas
- Check GDPR implications for automatic rollback annotations in customer logs
- Link to existing rollout metrics dashboards for p95 and semantic regression

Unresolved questions to bring to sync
- Do we want separate risk budgets per region? per customer tier?
- How to represent composite budgets in release notes and audit logs?

End of draft
- This is intentionally iterative. Will convert to a prettier wireframe doc once we align on primary unit and preset definitions.
